tweets.text: Hopes that Senate Majority Leader Thune will hold a cloture vote on the Clarity Act this week are fading. From a procedural standpoint, he would need to file cloture on the motion to proceed today to set up a Thursday vote under Senate rules, but those involved in the process expect the Russia/Iran sanctions bill to take precedence. Attention is instead shifting to next week, with industry stakeholders telling me it is “imperative” for leadership to at least begin the cloture process before the August recess.
tweets.summary: Senate cloture vote on the crypto market-structure Clarity Act likely slips past August recess amid competing sanctions bill.

tweets.text: RT @StaniKulechov: Very interesting interview with SEC Commissioner Peirce on vaults, especially the distinction between vaults and onchain lending protocols. In lending protocols, smart contracts facilitate transactions without intermediaries (traditional DeFi pool model). Vaults, by contrast, allocate and invest third-party assets, acting as intermediaries, which prompted the discussion on vaults and regulation.
tweets.summary: SEC Commissioner Peirce distinguishes DeFi lending protocols from asset-managing vaults, which act as intermediaries raising regulatory questions.

tweets.text: WITHOUT CLARITY, if a crypto exchange goes bankrupt, customers’ assets (crypto, stocks, cash, etc) are at risk of being treated as the exchange’s property and used to pay off the company’s debts. Customers are treated as unsecured creditors. In sum, retail investors get screwed and remain without protection. CLARITY helps prevent that from happening. Quite possibly the best advertisement for passing Clarity is that @ewarren is against it at the federal level and Letitia James is against it at the state level. Must be worth passing.
tweets.summary: Deaton argues the CLARITY Act protects crypto exchange customers from being treated as unsecured creditors in bankruptcy.

tweets.text: RT @CJRobins01: Over the last week, our small but mighty @Morpho team met with nearly a dozen Senate offices to talk about the Clarity Act. The message we heard in every meeting was "we're trying to get to yes." That's encouraging, because the Clarity Act is a massive opportunity for the US to lead on the regulation of digital asset markets, and its a massive improvement over the status quo. Here's what the status quo actually looks like: 1️⃣ The industry lacks oversight. A lack of regulatory clarity favors bad actors, who take advantage of the uncertainty to exploit consumers. If we don't move now, we're leaving the door open to more bad actors. 2️⃣ The industry lacks transparency. Without mandated disclosures and listing standards, consumers are regularly exposed to scams and frauds. 3️⃣ The industry lacks standards. Without standards around decentralization and control, consumers are exposed to unknown risks when using blockchain networks. Is the bill perfect? No. But no bill is perfect, and we can't let perfection be the enemy of progress. The @BlockchainAssn launched https://t.co/nz8glv3BGl, which is a website that helps companies, constituents, and voters urge Senate leadership to bring the Clarity Act to the floor. Let's get this across the line!
tweets.summary: Morpho lobbied Senate offices to advance the Clarity Act for US digital asset market regulation.
